text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- The goverment wants to end illegal, non-contract working. Companies will be given one month to either give workers a proper contract or lay them off, according to Labour Ministry instruction.
- With favorable forecasts from the Bank of Portugal, conditions are right for Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco to announce a cut in personal incomes and social security payments for 1998.
- Government is preparing legislation to toughen penalties for companies that flaunt labour laws.
- European Commission says Portugal is one of the countries best placed to fulfil Maastricht criteria. Unemployment may fall during next few years, but a rise on the number of long term unemployed.

- The IMF puts Portugal on track to join the single currency, forecasting a budget deficit of 2.9 percent of gross domestic product and inflation of 2.5 percent to 1997, and 2.5 and 2.3 percent, respectively, in 1998.
